A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Log-Linear Attention work. The complete text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable, and relocated material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: V1 reports original MQAR experiments, implementation benchmarks, language-model training and evaluations on recall, reasoning and long-context tasks.

after.justification: V3 retains original language-model and implementation results and reports revised MQAR experiments and an additional Hyena comparison.

M1.justification: The Fenwick-tree memory partition, input-dependent bucket weights, recurrent updates, chunkwise algorithm and Mamba-2/Gated DeltaNet constructions are retained. Revised explanations and MQAR tuning do not establish a change to the proposed procedure; the tensor generalization also remains in Appendix A.

E1.justification: Both versions use MQAR, Long-Data-Collections pretraining, standard language-model and commonsense benchmarks, Book3, RULER NIAH, retrieval tasks and LongBench. Retrieval and LongBench results move to the appendix. MQAR length and model-configuration changes revise the protocol within the retained task.

E2.justification: The MQAR comparison replaces non-gated DeltaNet with Mamba-2 and Gated DeltaNet and their log-linear variants; Transformer remains the full-attention reference. V3 also actually evaluates a parameter-matched Hyena model on WikiText, adding a log-linear-compute comparator beyond the original experimental families.

E3.justification: V1 reports MQAR training for 100 epochs on 10K examples, varying sequence length with one key-value pair per four tokens and dimensions 16/32. V3 uses 256-token sequences with 4–64 pairs, dimensions 16/32/64, early stopping above 99% accuracy, lambda-parameterization tuning and model-specific head configurations. This substantially replaces the synthetic evaluation design; the main language-model protocol is retained.

E4.justification: V1 Figure 5 tests recall degradation as sequence length and retrieval load increase. V3 replaces these curves with fixed-length comparisons across model widths in Table 2 and Figure 9. The per-position-loss analysis, implementation comparisons and strong-versus-weak admissibility analysis remain.

E5.justification: V3 introduces five-seed MQAR reporting with average accuracies and standard deviations, whereas v1 supplies no corresponding uncertainty or run-count information. V3 also explicitly discloses that the large language models were run only once. These are changes in statistical reporting, not evidence that v1 used fewer runs.

E6.justification: MQAR results are replaced under the revised conditions, and Hyena WikiText perplexity 29.50 is added. Detailed language-model, NIAH, retrieval and LongBench scores remain unchanged. V3 Table 3 nevertheless reports Log-Linear Gated DeltaNet values 21.45/18.09/45.5 for WikiText perplexity, LAMBADA perplexity and average accuracy, versus 21.44/18.08/45.6 in both v1 Table 2 and v3 Table 6. This discrepancy does not establish a same-setting performance change.

T1.justification: V3 revises the chunkwise decomposition in Equation 5 to include gated-mask factors and an explicit chunk-aligned starting level. It also removes v1 Section 2's mathematical factorization for rank-one matrix-valued gates. The core recurrence, complexity arguments and mathematical developments in Appendices A–B are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central contribution: a general attention framework with logarithmically growing memory, log-linear training computation and Mamba-2/Gated DeltaNet instantiations that perform well relative to their linear counterparts.

C2.justification: V3 explicitly frames the experiments as demonstrating promise rather than establishing the best subquadratic architecture, discloses single-run language-model evidence and discusses possible xLSTM/MesaNet extensions. The explanatory summaries of retrieval and LongBench findings are removed while their results remain. Existing engineering and partitioning limitations are retained.

D1.justification: Appendix D adds MQAR-specific state/head dimensions, model-dependent head counts and tuning information. The revised setup no longer supplies v1's explicit epoch and sample counts. Existing implementation code, kernel optimizations, language-model training details, hardware information and code-access link remain.

R1.justification: V3 expands related work to include LogSparse Transformer, Informer, Treeformer, BP-Transformer, dilated convolutions and concurrent prefix-scannable models, and discusses xLSTM/MesaNet as future extensions. The earlier Sun et al. test-time-training citation disappears. These additions broaden context without redefining the central research positioning.

P1.justification: Section 3 substantially rewrites the method motivation, partitioning and training explanations and gives decoding its own subsection. The main-text generalizations subsection disappears while its appendix treatments remain; experimental and related-work narratives are reorganized, and an LLM-usage appendix is added.

P2.justification: The experimental presentation is substantially reorganized: MQAR gains a new table and replacement plot, language-model results gain a compact summary table, the NIAH table moves into the main text, and detailed language-model, retrieval and LongBench tables move into the appendix. These changes accompany the conference layout conversion; most retained technical diagrams and performance plots are unchanged.

improvement.justification: Five-seed MQAR statistics, comparisons with both principal model families, the Hyena baseline and clearer method exposition make v3 more informative and assessable. The gains are limited: large-model validation is unchanged, the former MQAR length-stress curves are lost, and Tables 3 and 6 introduce inconsistent summary scores. Overall, the added evidence and transparency provide a modest net improvement.
